Q: check if index a primary key in mysql A:

One nice and accessible way would be to simply use:

SHOW CREATE TABLE yourTable;

But this will also show the entire table definition. If you want something more focused, then use:

SHOW INDEX FROM yourTable;

Then find the primary index (and there should only be one).

Q: How to resolve this dependency conflict after a fresh install of Qwik (`npm create qwik@latest`)? A:

The error is caused by the recent release of eslint@10.0.0.

The workaround is to revise the @eslint/js version specification (which is currently latest) in devDependencies in package.json. I suggest specifying it to be ^9, though theoretically any number below 10.0.0 will serve to be an effective workaround.

Example workaround in package.json:

"devDependencies": {
...
    "@eslint/js": "^9",
...
},

I have made the Qwik dev team aware of this workaround here.

Q: Custom x64 Windows PE Not Running A:

I WAS ABLE TO FIND THE ISSUE!
the problem was never in the file alignment or rva alignment, it simply because of me not filling in the field for the major and minor subsystem version, in the optional header section, i filled it in and now the exe finally runs, so for anyone who is crazy like me and wants to craft exe's byte by byte, make sure to not forget the major and minor subsystem values!

fixed code

bits 64
;==== DOS HEADER ==== offset 0x00
dw "MZ"
times 29 dw 0
dd 0x80 ;e_lfanew offset 0x3C
times 16 dd 0

; ==== PE HEADER ==== 
db "PE", 0 , 0

;COFF HEADER
dw 0x8664 ;machine type
dw 0x01 ;number of sections
dd 0 ;timestamp
dd 0 ;pointer to symbols
dd 0 ;number of symbols
dw 0xF0 ;size of optional header
dw 0x22

;OPTIONAL HEADER                                       
dw 0x020B
db 0 ;major linker version
db 0 ;minor linker version
dd 0x200 ;size of code
dd 0;size of init data
dd 0 ; size of unint data
dd 0x1000 ;address of entry
dd 0x1000 ;base of code
dq 0x0 ;image base
dd 0x1000 ;section alignment
dd 0x200 ;file alignment
dw 0 ;major os version
dw 0 ;minor os version
dw 0 ;major image version
dw 0 ;minor image version
dw 0x06 ;major subsytem version
dw 0 ;minor subsystem version
dd 0 ;win32 version value
dd 0x2000 ;size of image
dd 0x200 ;size of headers 
dd 0 ;checksum
dw 0x03 ;subsystem console
dw 0x0160 ;dll characteristics
dq 0x100000 ;stack reserve
dq 0x1000 ;stack commit
dq 0x100000 ;heap reserv
dq 0x1000 ;heap commit
dd 0  ;loader flags
dd 0x10
times 16 dq 0

;SECTION HEADER
db ".text", 0, 0, 0
dd 0x04 ;virtual size 
dd 0x1000 ;virtual address
dd 0x200 ;size of raw data
dd 0x200 ;pointer to raw data
dd 0 ;pointer to relocation
dd 0 ;pointer to line numbers
dw 0 ;number of relocations
dw 0 ;number of line number
dd 0x60000020 ;characteristics
times 10 dq 0

.text:
    push 7
    pop rax
    ret
    times 63 dq 0
    dd 0

Q: Firebird datetime format A:

Since the VTS function reportedly returns textual data (but CHARACTER SET NONE is really fragile and would likely cause problems in future! ) you now can manipulate that text with string functions without looking into what that text mean.

See string functions at http://www.firebirdtest.com/file/documentation/reference_manuals/fblangref25-en/html/fblangref25-functions-scalarfuncs.html

It is not quite clear which of many formats you quoted you really want.

select datetime with this specific format (MM-DD-YYYY HH:mm).
Needed result (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm):

We would stick with the latter as you quoted it twice in the question.

Next question whether you want to get text or date form the server. Supposedly you want to have a formatted text as SQL server output, not the native date value.

Then you need to do three steps with the values like '20170816000001.3710000'.

  1. Remove all the digits past the YYYYMMDD part.
  2. Separate DD, MM and YYYY parts with dashes
  3. Append " 00:00" to the string.

Step 1:

 select Left('20170816000001.3710000', 8) from rdb$Database

 "20170816"

Step 2: 

select Overlay(
  Overlay(
     Left('20170816000001.3710000', 8)
     PLACING '-' FROM 7 FOR 0)
  PLACING '-' FROM 5 FOR 0)
from rdb$Database

"2017-08-16"

Step 3:

select Overlay( Overlay( Left('20170816000001.3710000', 8)
  PLACING '-' FROM 7 FOR 0) PLACING '-' FROM 5 FOR 0) || ' 00:00'
from rdb$Database

"2017-08-16 00:00"

However usually it is wrong idea to convert Date to text at SQL server level. Normally you return plain Date value form the server, and it is your application that should format that date into any text format of your choice.

select cast(
  Overlay( Overlay(
     Left('20170816000001.3710000', 8)
     PLACING '-' FROM 7 FOR 0) PLACING '-' FROM 5 FOR 0) 
  as date )
from rdb$Database
